summary: PaceForge maintains a strong security posture. The codebase demonstrates solid defensive practices with defense-in-depth architecture. Two minor vulnerabilities identified (one medium, one low); all critical attack surfaces protected.

vulnerabilities.title: Garmin login failure includes exception details in Telegram
vulnerabilities.description: Exception details including full error messages are sent via Telegram notification during Garmin authentication failures. While restricted to authenticated Telegram tokens only, this could leak implementation details to an observer with access to the Telegram chat.
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-209: Information Exposure Through an Error Message
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: An authenticated user with knowledge of PaceForge implementation could trigger a Garmin login 429 (rate limit) response and observe the full error message in Telegram, potentially learning about internal retry logic or rate-limit thresholds.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Sanitize Telegram messages to user-friendly text while preserving full details in server logs. Example: 'Garmin sign-in failed. Check your credentials and ensure your network connection is stable. Full error logged for troubleshooting.'

vulnerabilities.title: Misleading sessionStorage lifetime hint
vulnerabilities.description: UI hint states 'Stored locally, never committed' but tokens are actually in sessionStorage (volatile), not localStorage. This creates ambiguity about token lifecycle — specifically, that sessionStorage is cleared when the browser session ends.
vulnerabilities.affected_code: Hint text does not clarify sessionStorage volatile nature
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-454: External Entity in XML Document ('XXE') — N/A; actually CWE-656: Incorrect Handling of Sensitive Data
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: User believes token persists on-disk ('locally') and doesn't close the browser, leaving the tab open — they expect the token to still be there the next day. While sessionStorage actually clears on tab/browser close, the ambiguous hint could lead to incorrect assumptions about token security.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Update hint text to clarify: 'Stored in your browser session only — cleared when you close the browser or all tabs. Refresh the page and re-enter your token if needed.'

strengths.finding: Scrypt hashing with strong parameters (n=2^14, r=8, p=1)
strengths.impact: Resistant to GPU/ASIC attacks; ~100ms computation time per attempt

strengths.finding: Constant-time password comparison prevents timing attacks
strengths.verification: scripts/runner.py:778-779 — hmac.compare_digest() for both username and password
strengths.impact: Attacker cannot extract password via timing analysis

strengths.finding: HTTP body size capped at 1 MiB on unauthenticated login endpoint
strengths.verification: scripts/runner.py:814, 837 — MAX_BODY limit enforced; test at line 130-135
strengths.impact: Prevents unbounded memory allocation from Content-Length header abuse

strengths.finding: Session cookie security flags correctly set
strengths.impact: JavaScript cannot access cookie; transmitted over HTTPS only; CSRF-protected

strengths.finding: Path traversal blocked via is_relative_to() checks
strengths.impact: Symlink escape and directory traversal attacks blocked on /data/ and /web/

strengths.finding: Failed login attempts serialized with global lock (1s delay per attempt)
strengths.impact: Brute-force attack rate: max 60 attempts/minute, even with parallel connections

strengths.finding: No hardcoded secrets; all sensitive config via environment variables
strengths.verification: .env.example contains template only; all secrets in ~/.config/paceforge/env
strengths.impact: Secrets cannot leak via accidental git commits

strengths.finding: XML parser safe from XXE; only standard entities decoded
strengths.verification: web/bike/workouts.js:decodeEntities() — hardcoded ENTITIES map, no external DTD
strengths.impact: No XXE, entity expansion, or external entity resolution vulnerabilities

strengths.finding: No SQL injection surface (JSON-based file storage, no database queries)
strengths.verification: All data persisted via JSON; no SQL queries in codebase
strengths.impact: Entire class of SQL injection attacks eliminated

strengths.finding: DOM manipulation uses textContent, not innerHTML
strengths.verification: web/bike/view.js — textContent used for untrusted strings; escHtml() for HTML context
strengths.impact: Injected script tags cannot execute; stored XSS prevented

strengths.finding: Garmin credentials routed through WARP proxy; never logged
strengths.verification: scripts/runner.py:220, 263 — WARP socks5 proxy; credentials only in memory during handshake
strengths.impact: Garmin OAuth2 credentials not exposed to logs or ISP-level eavesdropping

strengths.finding: Strava/intervals.icu API tokens stored in volatile sessionStorage only
strengths.verification: web/bike/view.js:243 — sessionStorage, never localStorage or IndexedDB
strengths.impact: Tokens cleared on browser session end; not persisted to disk

strengths.finding: Numeric ranges enforced on all user inputs (RPE 1-10, power 0-2000, FTP 50-600, etc.)
strengths.impact: Prevents invalid state that could corrupt analytics or confuse training load calculations

strengths.finding: Trust boundary correctly enforced at accepting socket, not client headers
strengths.verification: scripts/runner.py:852 — INTERNAL_PORT check comes before any header parsing; test:79-83
strengths.impact: Forged X-Forwarded-For or other headers cannot bypass auth

strengths.finding: XML/HTML library versions specified (not pinned, allowing patch updates)
strengths.verification: pyproject.toml — requests, urllib3, cryptography all allow patch-level updates
strengths.impact: Security patches for dependencies can be pulled without manual intervention

protections: Returns login form; no data leakage
1 MiB body size cap (prevents DoS via Content-Length)
Data transformation functions validate all inputs before use
Path traversal check (is_relative_to on data/ only)
Never logged or persisted (memory-only during handshake)
Token auto-saved by library (not server code)
Egress via WARP (IP isolation from Garmin's rate-limit enforcement)
No refresh mechanism (manual re-entry after expiry)
Base64 encoding (not encryption; should not be relied on)

sql_injection.notes: No SQL queries anywhere in codebase. All data persisted via JSON files and Pydantic models. File-based storage eliminates this entire class of attacks.

xxe_entity_expansion.notes: Custom XML parser in web/bike/workouts.js only handles standard entities (amp, lt, gt, quot, apos) and numeric entities. No external DTD resolution, no entity expansion. XXE fully mitigated.

csrf.notes: All authenticated endpoints require session cookie (SameSite=Lax). CSRF tokens not needed for JSON API. Preflight checks block cross-origin form POSTs.

hardcoded_credentials.notes: .env.example is template only. All actual secrets in ~/.config/paceforge/env (Victor's) or ~/.config/paceforge/<name>.env (per-athlete instances). No credentials in git history or codebase.

password_handling.notes: Passwords never logged. Hashed with scrypt (n=2^14, r=8, p=1). Constant-time comparison via hmac.compare_digest(). Credentials only exist in memory during login POST; immediately discarded after verification.

xss.notes: DOM manipulation uses textContent for untrusted input. HTML rendering uses escHtml() helper. SVG color values are hardcoded from COGGAN_ZONES, not user-controlled. No eval(), no innerHTML with untrusted data.

path_traversal.notes: Both /data/ and /web/ routes use is_relative_to() to enforce directory boundaries. Symlink escape and ..-based traversal blocked. Verified in tests: test_contents_route_blocks_path_traversal, test_static_route_blocks_path_traversal.

dos_mitigation.notes: HTTP body limited to 1 MiB (line 814). Login attempts rate-limited to 1/second globally. HTTP socket timeout default 30s. Garmin rate-limit handling retries every 45min (non-blocking). SVG trace rebuild optimized (no N² behavior on current code).

authentication.notes: Scrypt-based with industry-standard parameters. Session cookie with HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax. Internal port trusts loopback-only connection; public port requires session. Trust boundary correct.

authorization.notes: Session-based. INTERNAL_PORT (timers, curl) bypasses auth by design (loopback-only, trusted). Public PORT requires session for all data endpoints. No privilege tiers (single-athlete app). Garmin login stores email in token-meta.json; re-login on new athlete uses updated email.

authentication_authorization.notes: Strong: scrypt + constant-time comparison. Two minor issues: (1) Garmin exception detail leakage (medium), (2) sessionStorage hint ambiguity (low). Both addressed in recommendations.

injection_attacks.notes: No SQL injection (JSON-based). No XXE (standard entities only). No command injection (subprocess.run with fixed argv). No HTML injection (textContent used). XSS fully mitigated.

sensitive_data_exposure.notes: Good: sessionStorage for API tokens (cleared on browser close), WARP proxy for Garmin handshake. One caveat: Garmin exception messages expose details (V001). Local user could inspect sessionStorage if device compromised.

broken_access_control.notes: Path traversal blocked. Trust boundary correct (socket-based, not header-based). Internal port properly isolated. CORS not needed (single-origin SPA).

insecure_dependencies.notes: Minor: loose version constraints in pyproject.toml allow automatic patch updates (good for security, can break compatibility). No known CVEs in transitive dependencies as of audit date.

denial_of_service.notes: HTTP body capped (1 MiB). Login rate-limited (1s delay). Garmin rate-limit resilience built in. Socket timeout configured. RUNS list can grow unbounded (noted in performance audit) but is in-memory only and resets on restart.

configuration_security.notes: No hardcoded secrets. All sensitive config in env files (0600 permissions). .env.example is template only.

recommendations.title: Sanitize Garmin error messages in Telegram
recommendations.description: Garmin login failures currently include full exception text. Sanitize to user-friendly messages while preserving detail in logs.
recommendations.fix_code:
Replace: telegram(f'🏃 PaceForge: Garmin sign-in failed — {msg}')
With: telegram('🏃 PaceForge: Garmin sign-in failed. Check your credentials and network connectivity. Full error logged.')
Then log full details to server logs: run.log(f'Garmin error: {msg}')
recommendations.impact: Reduces info-disclosure surface for authenticated observers

recommendations.title: Clarify sessionStorage lifetime in UI hints
recommendations.description: Current hint 'Stored locally, never committed' is ambiguous about volatile nature. Update to clarify browser session scope.
recommendations.fix_code: In web/bike/view.js line 244, update hint to: 'Stored in your browser session only — cleared when you close the browser or all tabs.'
recommendations.impact: Prevents user confusion about token persistence

recommendations.title: Add OAuth2 token refresh for Strava/intervals.icu
recommendations.description: Current implementation requires manual token re-entry after expiry. Implement automatic refresh via OAuth2 code exchange.
recommendations.fix_code: Store refresh_token in sessionStorage alongside access_token. Implement token refresh function that exchanges refresh_token for new access_token before making API calls.
recommendations.impact: Reduces user friction; eliminates manual token management

recommendations.title: Implement log rotation for sync logs
recommendations.description: Run logs in STATE_DIR accumulate unbounded (noted in performance audit). Implement rotation to keep last N runs.
recommendations.fix_code: In runner.py:main(), after loading runs from runs.jsonl, trim RUNS to last 500. Before each finish(), check RUNS length and truncate if > 1000.
recommendations.impact: Prevents unbounded disk usage from log accumulation; improves startup time

conclusion: PaceForge maintains a strong security posture for a single-athlete fitness coaching application. The two identified vulnerabilities are minor in scope (one informational, one UI clarity) and do not represent security breaches. All critical attack surfaces are protected against SQL injection, XSS, path traversal, and DoS attacks. No hardcoded secrets. Recommended fixes are refinements to already-safe behavior. Risk score 18/100 reflects comprehensive protective measures with only two low-impact issues for remediation.
